title: Cohomology commutes with extension of scalars along a field extension
statement:
Let $K\subset L$ be fields and let $C=(C^r,d^r)$ be a cochain complex of $K$-vector spaces, with cohomology modules $\mathrm H^i(C)$ [def-weil-derived-category-cohomology-functor]. Let $C\otimes_KL$ be the complex of $L$-vector spaces with terms $C^r\otimes_KL$ and differentials $d^r\otimes_KL$ (extension of scalars termwise [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension]). Then for every integer $i$ the $L$-linear map

$$
\mathrm H^i(C)\otimes_KL\longrightarrow\mathrm H^i(C\otimes_KL),\qquad[x]\otimes\lambda\longmapsto[x\otimes\lambda],
$$

is well defined and an isomorphism of $L$-vector spaces, natural in $C$ (compatible with the maps induced by morphisms of complexes). In particular, $C\otimes_KL$ has finite-dimensional cohomology over $L$ when $C$ has finite-dimensional cohomology over $K$, and a quasi-isomorphism $C\to C'$ of complexes of $K$-vector spaces induces a quasi-isomorphism $C\otimes_KL\to C'\otimes_KL$. For a tower $K\subset L\subset M$ the isomorphisms are compatible with the canonical isomorphisms $(V\otimes_KL)\otimes_LM\cong V\otimes_KM$ of [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension]: the square formed by $\mathrm H^i(C)\otimes_KM$, $(\mathrm H^i(C)\otimes_KL)\otimes_LM$, $\mathrm H^i(C\otimes_KL)\otimes_LM$ and $\mathrm H^i((C\otimes_KL)\otimes_LM)\cong\mathrm H^i(C\otimes_KM)$ commutes.

source.place: Stacks Project, Algebra, Section 'Flat modules' (Tag 00H9), Definition 00HB (M flat: −⊗_R M exact) — L is a free K-module (a K-basis exists), hence flat; Homology, Lemma 010N (exact functors between abelian categories) and the definition of H^i of a cochain complex in Section 'Complexes' (Tag 010V): an exact additive functor preserves kernels and images, hence carries Ker(d^i)/Im(d^{i-1}) to Ker(F d^i)/Im(F d^{i-1}). The blueprint uses this without a name in the stagewise definition of $\mathrm H^i$ on $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)$

proof.text: Fix $i\in\mathbf Z$ and put $Z^i=\ker d^i$ and $B^i=\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}$, so $\mathrm H^i(C)=Z^i/B^i$ by [def-weil-derived-category-cohomology-functor]. The termwise tensor maps of [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension] give a complex, since $(d^{r+1}\otimes1)(d^r\otimes1)=(d^{r+1}d^r)\otimes1=0$. If $x\in Z^i$, then $d(x\otimes\lambda)=dx\otimes\lambda=0$. Replacing $x$ by $x+d^{i-1}y$ changes $x\otimes\lambda$ by the boundary $d^{i-1}(y\otimes\lambda)$. Thus $([x],\lambda)\mapsto[x\otimes\lambda]$ is well defined on $\mathrm H^i(C)\times L$. It is additive in each variable and $K$-balanced, since $[ax\otimes\lambda]=[x\otimes a\lambda]$. The tensor universal property therefore gives the asserted map $\beta^i_{C,L}:\mathrm H^i(C)\otimes_KL\to\mathrm H^i(C\otimes_KL)$. It is $L$-linear because $[x\otimes a\lambda]=a[x\otimes\lambda]$ for $a\in L$.

source.place: Tag 010V (section-complexes), cochain cohomology as cycles modulo boundaries; algebra.tex Tag 00CV (section-tensor-product), balanced tensor universal property

proof.text: By [lem-weil-field-scalar-extension-exact], $F_L=-\otimes_KL:\operatorname{Mod}_K\to\operatorname{Mod}_L$ is additive and preserves finite limits and finite colimits, for arbitrary vector spaces. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to this functor and $C$. Its isomorphism $c^i_C:\mathrm H^i(C\otimes_KL)\to\mathrm H^i(C)\otimes_KL$ is compatible with cycles and their projections to cohomology. In particular the tensored cycle $x\otimes\lambda$ is sent to $[x]\otimes\lambda$, so $c^i_C\beta^i_{C,L}$ fixes every $[x]\otimes\lambda$. Every cohomology class has a cycle representative and pure tensors span a tensor product, so $c^i_C\beta^i_{C,L}=1$. Since $c^i_C$ is an isomorphism, $\beta^i_{C,L}=(c^i_C)^{-1}$, and hence is an isomorphism. This argument uses only the three terms in degrees $i-1,i,i+1$, and needs neither boundedness nor finite-dimensional terms.

source.place: Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor), preservation of kernels and cokernels; the induced homology comparison applied to the three-term complex in degree i

proof.text: For a morphism of complexes $f:C\to C'$, the induced cohomology map is $[x]\mapsto[f^i(x)]$ by [def-weil-derived-category-cohomology-functor], and its scalar extension acts on pure tensors as in [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension]. The two naturality composites from $\mathrm H^i(C)\otimes_KL$ to $\mathrm H^i(C'\otimes_KL)$ both send $[x]\otimes\lambda$ to $[f^i(x)\otimes\lambda]$. Since pure tensors span, the composites agree. Thus the isomorphisms of Step 2 are natural in $C$.

source.place: Tag 010V (section-complexes), formula for the induced cohomology map

proof.text: If $\mathrm H^i(C)$ is finite-dimensional over $K$, its scalar extension is finite-dimensional over $L$ by the basis assertion in [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension]. The isomorphism of Step 2 identifies that scalar extension with $\mathrm H^i(C\otimes_KL)$, proving the finite-dimensionality assertion degree by degree. No finiteness condition on the terms of $C$ is used.

source.place: Tag 05G5 (lemma-base-change-finiteness), finite modules remain finite under base change; basis extension for fields

proof.text: Let $f:C\to C'$ be a quasi-isomorphism. By [def-weil-derived-category-cohomology-functor], every $\mathrm H^i(f)$ is an isomorphism. Its tensor extension is an isomorphism: tensoring its inverse gives an inverse by functoriality in [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension]. The naturality square of Step 3 expresses $\mathrm H^i(f\otimes_KL)$ as this tensor extension conjugated by the two isomorphisms $\beta^i_{C,L}$ and $\beta^i_{C',L}$. It too is an isomorphism, for every $i$. This is exactly the definition of $f\otimes_KL$ being a quasi-isomorphism.

For $K\subset L\subset M$, let $\tau_V:(V\otimes_KL)\otimes_LM\to V\otimes_KM$ be the tower isomorphism of [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension], $(v\otimes\lambda)\otimes\mu\mapsto v\otimes\lambda\mu$. Its inverse sends $v\otimes\nu$ to $(v\otimes1)\otimes\nu$: the two composites are identities because $(v\otimes1)\otimes\lambda\mu=(v\otimes\lambda)\otimes\mu$ by $L$-balancing. Applied termwise it is a chain isomorphism $\tau_C$, since both $d\tau_C$ and $\tau_Cd$ send $(x\otimes\lambda)\otimes\mu$ to $dx\otimes\lambda\mu$. Apply the cohomology functor of [def-weil-derived-category-cohomology-functor] to $\tau_C$; its inverse is the cohomology of $\tau_C^{-1}$. On the common source $(\mathrm H^i(C)\otimes_KL)\otimes_LM$, compare the direct composite $\beta^i_{C,M}\circ\tau_{\mathrm H^i(C)}$ and the successive composite $\mathrm H^i(\tau_C)\circ\beta^i_{C\otimes_KL,M}\circ(\beta^i_{C,L}\otimes_LM)$. On $([x]\otimes\lambda)\otimes\mu$ the first gives $[x\otimes\lambda\mu]$; the second gives first $[x\otimes\lambda]\otimes\mu$, then $[(x\otimes\lambda)\otimes\mu]$, then $[x\otimes\lambda\mu]$. Here $\beta^i_{C\otimes_KL,M}$ is Step 1 for the $L$-complex $C\otimes_KL$ and the extension $L\subset M$. Nested pure tensors span the source, so the two $M$-linear maps agree. This is the asserted tower square after its canonical associativity identifications.
